title: Who was that handsome man?
scope: Past tense था, थी, थे, थीं; तो “so, as for”; comparison with से, ज़्यादा, कम, सब से; को constructions (मुझ को ज़ुकाम है, पसंद, मालूम); कि clauses; the vocative case

gloss.तो: after a word, sets it against something else (“as for …, at least”); at the start of a sentence it means “so”
gloss.कि: “that”, introducing the clause that follows; English often leaves it out

lessons.title: था, थी, थे, थीं
lessons.desc: “Was” and “were”: the past tense shows gender

items.q: Fill the gap: “Yesterday I was in the market. (a woman speaking)”
items.say: कल मैं बाज़ार में थी ।
items.en: Yesterday[0] I[1] was[4] in[3] the market[2]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: था
था is masculine singular. A woman says मैं थी.
थीं is plural. मैं is one person, so a woman says मैं थी.
items.why: Unlike है, the past tense shows gender: मैं था (man), मैं थी (woman).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki was ill yesterday.”
items.say: पिंकी कल बीमार थी ।
wrong: था
था is masculine singular. Pinki is a woman.
थे
थे is masculine plural (also used for आप, तुम, हम and respected people).
items.why: One woman spoken of plainly takes थी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Both shops were closed.”
items.say: दोनों दुकानें बंद थीं ।
wrong: थी
थी is singular, but there are two shops.
थे
थे is masculine. दुकान is feminine.
items.why: दुकानें is feminine plural, so the verb is थीं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The samosas were very hot.”
items.say: समोसे बहुत गरम थे ।
wrong: था
था is singular, but समोसे is plural.
थीं is feminine. समोसा is masculine.
items.why: समोसे is masculine plural, so the verb is थे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mr Sharma was in Varanasi before.”
items.say: शर्मा जी पहले वाराणसी में थे ।
wrong: था
A respected man (शर्मा जी) takes the honorific plural थे, though he is one person.
थीं is feminine plural (also used for आप, तुम, हम and respected women). Mr Sharma is a man.
items.why: Respect works in the past as in the present: शर्मा जी … थे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where were you yesterday? (to a woman)”
items.say: आप कल कहाँ थीं ?
items.en: Where[2] were[3] you[0] yesterday[1]? (to a woman)
wrong: थी
आप is grammatically plural, so even for one woman the verb is थीं.
थे
थे is right for a man. A woman is asked आप … थीं ?
items.why: आप takes the plural: थे for a man, थीं for a woman.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We were out yesterday. (men speaking)”
items.say: हम लोग कल बाहर थे ।
wrong: था
था is singular, but हम लोग is plural.
थीं would be said by women. Men say हम थे.
items.why: हम is plural: थे for men or a mixed group, थीं for women.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The room was very dirty.”
items.say: कमरा बहुत गंदा था ।
wrong: थी
थी is feminine, but कमरा is masculine.
थे
थे is plural, but here कमरा is one room.
items.why: कमरा is masculine singular, like गंदा, so the verb is था.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These mountains were very high.”
items.say: ये पहाड़ बहुत ऊँचे थे ।
wrong: था
पहाड़ looks the same in the plural, but ये and ऊँचे show that it is plural here.
थीं is feminine. पहाड़ is masculine.
items.why: ये पहाड़ is masculine plural, so the verb is थे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where were the books?”
items.say: किताबें कहाँ थीं ?
wrong: थी
थी is singular, but किताबें is plural.
थे
थे is masculine. किताब is feminine.
items.why: किताबें is feminine plural, so the verb is थीं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Prakash was abroad before.”
items.say: प्रकाश पहले विदेश में था ।
wrong: थी
थी is feminine singular. Prakash is a man.
थीं is feminine plural (also used for आप, तुम, हम and respected women).
items.why: Prakash spoken of plainly takes था. विदेश में means “abroad”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan wasn't at the shop yesterday.”
items.say: मोहन कल दुकान पर नहीं था ।
wrong: थे
थे would show respect or a plural. Mohan spoken of plainly takes था.
थी
थी is feminine singular.
items.why: नहीं comes before the verb, as in the present: नहीं था.

items.q: Put this sentence into the past tense
wrong: लड़कियाँ बाहर थी ।
थी is singular, but लड़कियाँ is plural.
लड़कियाँ बाहर थे ।
थे is masculine. लड़की is feminine.
items.why: हैं becomes थीं for a feminine plural subject.
items.say: लड़कियाँ बाहर थीं ।

lessons.title: तो
lessons.desc: “So” at the start; contrast after a word

items.q: What does तो do at the start of this question?
items.a: It means “so, then” (तो at the start links to what was said before)
wrong: It contrasts आप with other people
That use puts तो after the word: आप तो …. At the start of a sentence तो means “so, then”.
It makes आप oblique
तो is not a postposition, so it never changes the case of the word before it.
items.why: At the beginning of a sentence or phrase, तो means “so” or “then”.
items.say: तो आप कल बीमार थे ?
items.en: So[0] were[4] you[1] ill[3] yesterday[2]? (to a man)

items.q: What does तो add after मैं here?
items.a: It contrasts “I” with Pinki: “I, for my part, was at college”
wrong: It means “so”, linking to the last sentence
तो means “so” only at the start. After a word it contrasts that word with something else.
It makes मैं oblique
तो is not a postposition, so it never changes the case of the word before it.
items.why: After a word or phrase, तो sets it against something else in the same context.
items.hi: मैं तो कालेज में थी, पर पिंकी बाहर थी ।
items.say: मैं तो कालेज में थी, पर पिंकी बाहर थी ।
items.en: I[0] was[4] at[3] college[2], but[5] Pinki[6] was[8] out[7]. (a woman speaking)

items.q: Fill the gap: “The room was big, but the garden was very small.”
items.hi: कमरा ___ बड़ा था, पर बग़ीचा बहुत छोटा था ।
items.say: कमरा तो बड़ा था, पर बग़ीचा बहुत छोटा था ।
items.en: The room[0] was[3] big[2], but[4] the garden[5] was[8] very[6] small[7].
wrong: भी
भी would say the room too was big, as well as something else. The sentence sets the room against the garden.
से
से is a postposition (“from, than”). It would need the oblique कमरे and makes no sense here.
items.why: तो after कमरा contrasts the room with the garden. तो is not a postposition, so it never changes the case of the word before it.

items.q: Is तो a postposition?
items.a: No, so the word before it stays in the direct case
wrong: Yes, so the word before it becomes oblique
Postpositions such as में and से make a word oblique. तो does not: कमरा तो, not कमरे तो.
Only when it comes first in the sentence
At the start तो means “so”. It never works as a postposition.
items.why: तो is not a postposition, so it never changes the case of the word before it.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Today the weather is good (on other days it isn't).
wrong: So the weather is good today?
“So” would put तो first: तो आज मौसम अच्छा है ? Here it follows आज and contrasts today with other days.
The weather is good today too.
“Too” is भी. तो sets today against other days.
items.why: तो after आज contrasts today with other days.

items.q: Fill the gap: “So where was Sita yesterday?”
items.say: तो सीता कल कहाँ थी ?
wrong: भी
भी means “too, also” and never comes first.
कि
कि (“that”) joins a clause to words like मालूम है. It does not open a question.
items.why: At the start of a sentence तो means “so, then”.

items.q: In मोहन तो बाज़ार में था, which word does तो contrast?
items.a: मोहन — Mohan was at the market, unlike the others
wrong: बाज़ार — the market, rather than somewhere else
To contrast the place, तो would follow it: बाज़ार में तो.
था — he was, but no longer is
तो points back at what comes just before it, here मोहन, not the verb था.
items.why: तो contrasts the word or phrase just before it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This palace is bigger than that palace.”
items.hi: यह महल उस महल ___ बड़ा है ।
items.say: यह महल उस महल से बड़ा है ।
items.en: This[0] palace[1] is[6] bigger[5] than[4] that[2] palace[3].
wrong: में means “in”. “Than” is से.
तक
तक means “up to, as far as”. “Than” is से.
items.why: Comparisons use से “than” after the thing compared against, and an ordinary adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My room is smaller than your room.”
items.hi: मेरा कमरा तुम्हारे ___ से छोटा है ।
items.say: मेरा कमरा तुम्हारे कमरे से छोटा है ।
items.en: My[0] room[1] is[6] smaller[5] than[4] your[2] room[3].
wrong: कमरा
कमरा is the direct form. Before से it is oblique: कमरे.
कमरों
कमरों is the oblique plural, “rooms”. The English says one room.
items.why: The noun before से is oblique, like any noun before a postposition.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki is younger than Prakash.”
items.say: पिंकी प्रकाश से छोटी है ।
wrong: छोटा
The adjective agrees with the subject, Pinki, not with Prakash.
छोटे
छोटे would be plural or respectful. Pinki spoken of plainly takes the singular.
items.why: The adjective agrees with the subject of the sentence. Of people, छोटा and बड़ा mean “younger” and “older”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This tea is less hot than that tea.”
items.hi: यह चाय उस चाय से ___ गरम है ।
items.say: यह चाय उस चाय से कम गरम है ।
items.en: This[0] tea[1] is[7] less[5] hot[6] than[4] that[2] tea[3].
wrong: ज़्यादा
ज़्यादा means “more”. “Less” is कम.
और
और before an adjective means “more”, the opposite of “less”.
items.why: कम “less” before the adjective gives “less … than”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj is the cleverest of all.”
items.say: राज सब से होशियार है ।
wrong: को
को means “to”. The superlative uses सब से.
तक
तक means “up to”. The superlative uses सब से.
items.why: सब से “than all” before an adjective makes the superlative.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My sister is older than me.”
items.say: मेरी बहिन मुझ से बड़ी है ।
items.en: My[0] sister[1] is[5] older[4] than[3] me[2].
wrong: मैं is the direct form. Before से it becomes मुझ.
मेरा
मेरा means “my”. Before से you need the pronoun itself, मुझ.
items.why: मैं becomes मुझ before a postposition, also before से “than”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This car is newer than those cars.”
items.hi: यह गाड़ी उन ___ से नई है ।
items.say: यह गाड़ी उन गाड़ियों से नई है ।
items.en: This[0] car[1] is[6] newer[5] than[4] those[2] cars[3].
wrong: गाड़ियाँ is the direct plural. Before से the oblique plural is needed.
गाड़ी
उन is plural, so the noun must be plural too.
items.why: The noun compared against is oblique before से — गाड़ियों.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Suhas is more hardworking than those tall boys.”
items.hi: सुहास उन ___ लड़कों से ज़्यादा मेहनती है ।
items.say: सुहास उन लंबे लड़कों से ज़्यादा मेहनती है ।
items.en: Suhas[0] is[7] more[5] hardworking[6] than[4] those[1] tall[2] boys[3].
wrong: लंबा
लंबा is the direct form. Its noun लड़कों is oblique, so the adjective is too.
लंबों
Adjectives never take -õ. Their -e form serves for the oblique plural.
items.why: An -ā adjective before an oblique noun takes -e.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The samosas were colder than the daal.”
items.say: समोसे दाल से ज़्यादा ठंडे थे ।
items.en: The samosas[0] were[5] colder[3+4] than[2] the daal[1].
wrong: ठंडी
ठंडी would agree with दाल. The adjective agrees with the subject, समोसे.
ठंडा
ठंडा is singular, but समोसे is plural.
items.why: The adjective agrees with the subject, here masculine plural समोसे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My book is older than your book. (to तुम)”
items.hi: मेरी किताब ___ किताब से ज़्यादा पुरानी है ।
items.say: मेरी किताब तुम्हारी किताब से ज़्यादा पुरानी है ।
items.en: My[0] book[1] is[7] older[5+6] than[4] your[2] book[3]. (to तुम)
wrong: तुम्हारे
-e is for masculine nouns. Feminine -ī forms never change, even before से.
तुम्हारा
तुम्हारा is masculine, but किताब is feminine.
items.why: The possessive agrees with किताब, feminine; -ī forms stay -ī in the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Delhi is my dearest city.”
items.hi: दिल्ली मेरा सब से ___ शहर है ।
items.say: दिल्ली मेरा सब से प्यारा शहर है ।
wrong: प्यारी
प्यारा describes शहर, which is masculine.
प्यारे
प्यारे is plural or oblique. शहर here is singular and direct.
items.why: In सब से प्यारा शहर the adjective agrees with शहर.

lessons.title: मुझ को ज़ुकाम है
lessons.desc: को constructions: the verb agrees with the thing

items.q: Fill the gap: “Uncle had a fever yesterday.”
items.say: चाचा जी को कल बुख़ार था ।
wrong: थे
Respect for चाचा जी does not matter here: the subject is बुख़ार, masculine singular.
थी
थी is feminine. बुख़ार is masculine.
items.why: In X को बुख़ार है the subject is बुख़ार, not the sufferer, so the verb agrees with बुख़ार.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother hopes that the children are at home.”
items.hi: माँ को आशा ___ कि बच्चे घर पर हैं ।
items.say: माँ को आशा है कि बच्चे घर पर हैं ।
items.en: Mother[0+1] hopes[2+3] that[4] the children[5] are[8] at[7] home[6].
wrong: The verb agrees with आशा, feminine singular, not with माँ, however respected.
हूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: In X को आशा है the subject is आशा.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki likes tea.”
items.say: पिंकी को चाय पसंद है ।
wrong: हैं would need a plural subject. The subject is चाय, the thing liked.
हो
हो goes only with तुम.
items.why: X को Y पसंद है is literally “Y is pleasing to X”: the verb agrees with Y.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita likes these old cars.”
items.hi: सीता को ये पुरानी गाड़ियाँ पसंद ___ ।
items.say: सीता को ये पुरानी गाड़ियाँ पसंद हैं ।
wrong: है
है would agree with Sita, but the subject is the thing liked, गाड़ियाँ, which is plural.
हो
हो goes only with तुम.
items.why: With पसंद the verb agrees with the thing liked.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I like this city a lot.”
items.hi: ___ को यह शहर बहुत पसंद है ।
items.say: मुझ को यह शहर बहुत पसंद है ।
wrong: मैं is the direct form. Before को it becomes मुझ. The subject here is शहर.
मेरा
मेरा means “my”. Before को you need the pronoun itself, मुझ.
items.why: The person who likes something is marked with को, so मैं becomes मुझ.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki is sorry that the shop is closed.”
items.hi: पिंकी को ___ है कि दुकान बंद है ।
items.say: पिंकी को अफ़सोस है कि दुकान बंद है ।
items.en: Pinki[0+1] {is sorry}[2+3] that[4] the shop[5] is[7] closed[6].
wrong: ख़ुशी
ख़ुशी is “happiness”: पिंकी को ख़ुशी है means “Pinki is glad”.
आशा
आशा is “hope”: पिंकी को आशा है means “Pinki hopes”.
items.why: X को अफ़सोस है is “X is sorry”, literally “to X there is regret”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita is glad that the college is closed tomorrow.”
items.hi: सीता को ___ है कि कालेज कल बंद है ।
items.say: सीता को ख़ुशी है कि कालेज कल बंद है ।
items.en: Sita[0+1] is[3] glad[2] that[4] the college[5] is[8] closed[7] tomorrow[6].
wrong: अफ़सोस
अफ़सोस is “regret”: सीता को अफ़सोस है means “Sita is sorry”.
ज़ुकाम
ज़ुकाम is “a cold”: सीता को ज़ुकाम है means “Sita has a cold”, and a cold cannot be about something.
items.why: X को ख़ुशी है कि … is “X is glad that …”. With a present-tense verb, कल means “tomorrow”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan doesn't know who Pinki is.”
items.hi: मोहन को ___ नहीं है कि पिंकी कौन है ।
items.say: मोहन को मालूम नहीं है कि पिंकी कौन है ।
wrong: पसंद
पसंद means “liked”. “Know” is मालूम, “known”.
ख़ुशी
ख़ुशी means “happiness”. “Know” is मालूम.
items.why: X को मालूम है is “X knows”, literally “to X it is known”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My brother has a fever.”
items.say: मेरे भाई को बुख़ार है ।
wrong: मेरा
मेरा is the direct form. भाई is oblique before को, so the possessive takes -e.
मेरी
मेरी is feminine, but भाई is masculine.
items.why: को is a postposition, so the sufferer and its possessive are oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These girls don't like tea.”
items.hi: इन ___ को चाय पसंद नहीं है ।
items.say: इन लड़कियों को चाय पसंद नहीं है ।
wrong: लड़कियाँ
लड़कियाँ is the direct plural. Before को the oblique plural is needed.
लड़की
इन is plural, so the noun must be plural too.
items.why: The person who likes takes को, so the noun is oblique: लड़कियों को.

items.q: In मोहन को समोसे पसंद हैं, what is the grammatical subject?
wrong: मोहन
Mohan is the one who likes, marked with को. The verb हैं agrees with समोसे, not with him.
पसंद
पसंद is an adjective, “pleasing”. It describes the subject, समोसे.
items.why: With पसंद the thing liked is the subject; the person is oblique with को.

items.q: Put this sentence into the past tense
wrong: बच्चों को बुख़ार थे ।
थे would agree with the children, but the subject is बुख़ार, masculine singular.
बच्चों को बुख़ार थी ।
थी is feminine. बुख़ार is masculine.
items.why: The verb agrees with बुख़ार, so है becomes था.
items.say: बच्चों को बुख़ार था ।

items.q: Which sentence means “Mother likes silver”?
wrong: माँ चाँदी पसंद है ।
Without को this does not say who likes it. The person who likes takes को.
माँ को चाँदी पसंद हैं ।
The verb agrees with चाँदी, which is singular. Respect for माँ does not change it.
items.why: X को Y पसंद है — Y is the subject, and the verb agrees with it.

lessons.title: मालूम है कि …
lessons.desc: Questions inside a sentence with कि

items.q: Which sentence means “Do you know where my glasses are?”
items.a: क्या आप को मालूम है कि मेरा चश्मा कहाँ है ?
wrong: क्या आप को मालूम है कि कहाँ मेरा चश्मा है ?
After कि the question keeps its own order, मेरा चश्मा कहाँ है ?, with nothing moved.
क्या आप मालूम हैं कि मेरा चश्मा कहाँ है ?
The person who knows takes को — आप को मालूम है.
items.why: The core question मेरा चश्मा कहाँ है ? stays unchanged after कि.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Does Pinki know how Suhas was yesterday?”
items.hi: क्या पिंकी को मालूम है ___ सुहास कल कैसा था ?
items.say: क्या पिंकी को मालूम है कि सुहास कल कैसा था ?
items.en: Does[0] Pinki[1+2] know[3+4] how[8] Suhas[6] was[9] yesterday[7]?
wrong: तो
तो means “so” or adds contrast. It does not join a clause to मालूम है.
और
और means “and”. A clause after मालूम है is joined with कि.
items.why: कि “that” introduces the clause after मालूम है. English often leaves it out.

items.q: In this sentence, the words after कि…
items.a: keep the order of the plain question, unchanged
wrong: are rearranged, as English rearranges “where was Pinki?”
English turns “where was Pinki?” into “where Pinki was”. Hindi leaves the core question पिंकी कल कहाँ थी ? as it is.
lose their verb
The verb थी stays. The words after कि are a full question.
items.why: The words after कि are the core question, unchanged.
items.hi: माँ को मालूम है कि पिंकी कल कहाँ थी ।
items.say: माँ को मालूम है कि पिंकी कल कहाँ थी ।
items.en: Mother[0+1] knows[2+3] where[7] Pinki[5] was[8] yesterday[6].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हम को मालूम है कि चाचा जी कल वाराणसी में थे ।
items.a: We know that Uncle was in Varanasi yesterday.
wrong: We know that Uncle will be in Varanasi tomorrow.
थे is past, so कल here means “yesterday”.
Does Uncle know that we were in Varanasi?
हम को मालूम है says “we know”. There is no क्या, and चाचा जी is the one in Varanasi.
items.why: कल means “yesterday” or “tomorrow”; the tense shows which.

lessons.title: बच्चो ! बेटे !
lessons.desc: The vocative case, for calling out

items.q: Fill the gap: “Children, the food is hot!”
items.say: बच्चो, खाना गरम है !
wrong: बच्चों
बच्चों, with a nasal, is the oblique plural, used before a postposition. Calling out to people uses -o without the nasal.
बच्चे
बच्चे is the direct plural. When you address people, the vocative is used.
items.why: The vocative is like the oblique, except that the plural ending -o has no nasal.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Son, you are very clever.”
items.say: बेटे, तुम बहुत होशियार हो ।
wrong: बेटा
बेटा is the direct form. Addressing someone uses the vocative, like the oblique: बेटे.
बेटो
बेटो is the vocative plural, for several sons.
items.why: A masculine noun in -ā takes -e in the vocative singular, as in the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Boys, the college is closed today.”
items.say: लड़को, आज कालेज बंद है ।
items.en: Boys[0], the college[2] is[4] closed[3] today[1].
wrong: लड़कों
लड़कों, with a nasal, is the oblique plural. The vocative plural has no nasal.
लड़के
लड़के is the direct plural, or the vocative of one boy.
items.why: The vocative is like the oblique, except that the plural ending -o has no nasal.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Girls, the tea is cold!”
items.say: लड़कियो, चाय ठंडी है !
wrong: लड़कियों
लड़कियों, with a nasal, is the oblique plural. The vocative plural has no nasal.
लड़कियाँ
लड़कियाँ is the direct plural. When you address people, the vocative is used.
items.why: Nouns in -ī take -iyo in the vocative plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Friends, this is my house.”
items.say: दोस्तो, यह मेरा घर है ।
wrong: दोस्तों
दोस्तों, with a nasal, is the oblique plural. The vocative plural has no nasal.
दोस्त
दोस्त is singular, “friend”. The English addresses several.
items.why: The vocative is like the oblique, except that the plural ending -o has no nasal.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Brothers, where were you yesterday?”
items.say: भाइयो, कल आप लोग कहाँ थे ?
wrong: भाइयों
भाइयों, with a nasal, is the oblique plural. Addressing people drops the nasal.
भाई
भाई is the direct form. The vocative plural is भाइयो.
items.why: भाई takes -iyo in the vocative plural: the -ī shortens, as in the oblique.

items.q: How is the vocative (the form for calling out to someone) made?
items.a: Like the oblique, but the plural ending is -o, without a nasal
wrong: Like the direct case
The direct case would give बेटा and बच्चे. The vocative gives बेटे and बच्चो.
Like the oblique, with the plural in -õ
-õ with a nasal is the oblique plural. The vocative plural has a plain -o: बच्चो, not बच्चों.
items.why: The vocative is like the oblique, except that the plural ending -o has no nasal.

wrong: था
दुकान is feminine, so the verb is थी.
थीं is plural, but there is one shop.
में means “in”. “Than” is से.
को
को means “to”. “Than” is से.
items.order: The one compared against comes just before से — सीता मोहन से होशियार है means Sita is cleverer than Mohan.

items.en: My[0] neighbour[1+2] has[4] a cold[3]. (a man)
wrong: मेरा
पड़ोसी is oblique before को, so the possessive takes -e: मेरे.
The verb agrees with ज़ुकाम, masculine singular.
है
The verb agrees with the thing liked, समोसे, which is plural.
दोस्तों
दोस्तों is the oblique plural, “friends”. The English says one friend.

items.en: Children[0], the samosas[1] are[4] very[2] hot[3]!
wrong: बच्चों
बच्चों is the oblique plural. Calling out to people uses the vocative बच्चो, without the nasal.
है
है is singular, but समोसे is plural.
पुरानी
पुरानी is feminine, but महल is masculine.
में means “in”. The superlative is सब से.

items.en: Does[0] Pinki[1+2] know[3+4] where[7] the tablets[6] are[8]?
wrong: थीं is past, “were”. The English says “are”.
कौन
कौन asks “who?”. “Where” is कहाँ.
items.order: After कि the core question keeps its own order: गोलियाँ कहाँ हैं ?

items.en: Prakash[0+1] was[5] in[4] the market[3] yesterday[2].
wrong: था
A respected man (प्रकाश जी) takes the honorific plural थे.
थीं is feminine. Prakash is a man.
थी
थी is singular, but लड़कियाँ is plural.
थे
थे is masculine. लड़की is feminine.

items.en: Is[5] Pinki[1] older[4] than[3] you[2]? (to तुम)
wrong: तुम्हारे
तुम्हारे means “your”. Before से the pronoun itself stays तुम.
बड़ा
बड़ा is masculine. The adjective agrees with the subject, Pinki.

items.en: This[0] room[1] is[7] less[5] airy[6] than[4] that[2] one[3].
wrong: वह
वह is the direct form. Before an oblique noun it becomes उस.
कमरों
कमरों is the oblique plural, “rooms”. The English compares with one room.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरा दोस्त मुझ से ज़्यादा होशियार है ।
items.a: My friend is cleverer than me.
wrong: I am cleverer than my friend.
The one before से is the one compared against: मुझ से “than me”.
My friend is very clever, like me.
मुझ से ज़्यादा means “more than me”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: It is very cold outside.
था is past, “was”. “Is” would be है.
It was very hot outside.
ठंडा means “cold”. “Hot” is गरम.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: पहले वाराणसी में मेरे कई रिश्तेदार थे ।
items.a: I used to have several relatives in Varanasi.
wrong: Several of my relatives are in Varanasi now.
पहले … थे is past: “previously … were”.
Several of my friends were in Varanasi before.
रिश्तेदार means “relative”. “Friend” is दोस्त.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: सीता को कल बुख़ार था, पर आज वह ठीक है ।
items.a: Sita had a fever yesterday, but today she is fine.
wrong: Sita has a fever today, but yesterday she was fine.
The fever goes with कल … था, and ठीक है with आज.
Sita had a cold yesterday, but today she is fine.
बुख़ार is “fever”. “A cold” is ज़ुकाम.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: ओ दोस्तो, यह बाज़ार सब से सस्ता है !
items.a: Oh friends, this market is the cheapest!
wrong: Oh friends, this market is cheaper than the others!
सब से before the adjective is the superlative, “the cheapest”.
Oh friend, all the markets are cheap!
दोस्तो is plural, and यह बाज़ार is one market. सब से सस्ता means “cheapest of all”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: क्या आप को यह खाना पसंद नहीं है ?
wrong: Do you like this food?
नहीं makes the question negative.
Don't you know this food?
मालूम means “known”. पसंद means “liked”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: यह महल सौ साल पुराना है ।
items.a: This palace is a hundred years old.
wrong: This palace is ten years old.
सौ is “hundred”. “Ten” is दस.
This mountain is a hundred years old.
महल is “palace”. “Mountain” is पहाड़.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: क्या तुम को मालूम है कि दुकान कल बंद थी ?
items.a: Do you know that the shop was closed yesterday?
wrong: Do you know whether the shop is closed tomorrow?
थी is past, so कल means “yesterday”.
Do you know why the shop was closed yesterday?
There is no क्यों “why” here. कि just means “that”.

lessons.title: Rules and usage
lessons.desc: Comparison, the past, कल and क्या

items.q: What does से mean in यह गाड़ी उस गाड़ी से सस्ती है ?
wrong: from
से can mean “from”, but after the thing compared against, with an adjective, it means “than”.
with
से can mean “with”, but in a comparison it means “than”.
items.why: Comparisons use से “than”. The adjective itself does not change.

items.q: Which word can mean “more” before the adjective in a comparison?
wrong: only ज़्यादा
और also means “more” before an adjective: और लंबा “taller”.
only बहुत
बहुत means “very”. “More” is ज़्यादा or और.
items.why: ज़्यादा or और before the adjective makes a comparison more specific; it is also used when “than whom” is not stated.

items.q: How does the past tense of “to be” differ from the present?
items.a: It shows gender as well as number
wrong: The past tense does not show number
था and थी are singular; थे and थीं are plural.
Both tenses show gender in the same way
है and हैं are the same for men and women. Only the past shows gender.
items.why: Unlike है, the past tense distinguishes masculine and feminine: था, थी, थे, थीं.

items.q: Which phrase means “of all” in a superlative?
wrong: सब को
को means “to”. The superlative uses सब से, “than all”.
सब तक
तक means “up to”. The superlative uses सब से.
items.why: सब से अच्छा, literally “better than all”, is “best”.

items.q: What does कल mean in कल मैं बीमार थी ?
wrong: tomorrow
कल means both “yesterday” and “tomorrow”. थी is past, so here it is “yesterday”.
today
“Today” is आज.
items.why: कल is “yesterday” or “tomorrow”; the tense of the verb shows which.

items.q: In casual speech, where else can the question word क्या go in a yes/no question?
items.a: At the very end: वह घर पर है क्या ?
wrong: Just before the verb: वह घर पर क्या है ?
That would ask “what is at home?”. Casual speech can move the yes/no क्या to the end.
Nowhere else: क्या must always come first
In casual speech the yes/no क्या is often put at the very end instead.
items.why: क्या normally starts a yes/no question, but in casual speech it is often added at the end.
